newsitem.title: UK: North Africa oil output to rise sharply by 2000 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: North Africa oil output to rise sharply by 2000 - IEA.

text.p: Efforts to attract foreign investors in a trio of north African countries should substantially boost crude oil and natural gas liquids (NGLs) production capacity by the turn of the century, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in a new report.
Together the three countries were implementing plans to increase crude production by 18 percent to 3.65 million barrels a day (bpd) in 2000, the Paris-based agency said.
But actual increases could prove far greater, it said.

Algeria, having invited the return of foreign companies in 1996, was set for a 200,000 bpd rise in crude capacity to one million bpd by 2000. NGLs capacity should rise to 655,000 bpd from 515,000 bpd.
But successful operations from all the foreign companies in Algeria could push crude capacity to as much as 1.5 million bpd, it added.
Libyan crude capacity would rise to 1.65 million bpd of crude from 1.4 million bpd last year, the report said.
But new seismic and production enhancement methods could boost production beyond those levels.
Egypt's crude capacity was likely to rise 100,000 bpd to one million with NGLs up 50,000 bpd to 110,000 bpd.
